questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: We did not have many universities to choose from, but choosing a university that is part of the EU has definitely made the process much easier.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Although the university was very large, there was good information and the university was very helpful with everything. Already in advance, there were several Zoom meetings with relevant information, and they were good at responding to emails

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Normally there would be people waiting in the airport at campus. But due to a later arrival this was not the situation for me. But they had a 24-hours welcome desk and everyone was wery helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: On the website it seems like more options were available. But yoy could give them a prioritied list and then you would (hopefully) be offered something.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: In the accomadation I stayed in we had a fully equipped kitchen, but no oven. You could borrow an oven in some of the shared social spaces around campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It was very expensive and old, but it is definitely worth it. You save a lot of transport time, and you also live with all the other exchange students, which is how I found my friends. They also host many free events (though you need to stay very updated).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are many steps and deadlines. You need to be very patient, but there is help available in many places.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: After being approved by KU, you need to secure a place at UCD. You will receive all the information you need.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Someone contacted me regarding course selection and another person contacted me regarding my bachelor's project. She became my contact person and was very helpful with all questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got my 1st and 2nd choices and my 4th choice instead of my 3rd choice. I got the bachelor's project I applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Talk to former students who have been there. Even if you read a course description, it can be very difficult to assess how demanding the different courses are.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As a pharmacy student, it was very new. You are well-prepared to go. However, you should be aware that their teaching approach is very different. The assignments you do during the semester often count towards your grade. Therefore, the workload is greater during the semester than it is at home, but it makes it less stressful at the end of the semester.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The approach to learning is very different and can therefore seem more difficult. However, the knowledge you have from KU is sufficient to follow their courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: They don't use textbooks in the same way but encourage you to find scientific articles to reference. Similarly, their lab reports are also structured that way.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
BMOL40330 Biomol. Sci. Research Project (Bachelor project)
BIOC40220 Hot topics in Biochemistry & Molecular Biology
PHAR30030 Toxicology
PHAR30040 Development and advanced pharmacology of the nervous system

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
BIOC40220 Hot topics in Biochemistry & Molecular Biology

This course had a very light workload and no exam. If you haven't done many presentations before, it can be good practice before presenting your bachelor's project. The entire course has a very relaxed approach.

questions.answer: Public transport was very cheap. Bars were very expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The campus has everything. Dublin offer a lot of good things. 
The campus need some grocery stores closer by.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university have a lot of sport clubs and societies. Everything you can think of.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There is so much pretty nature close to Dublin that can be reach by public transport.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go around Ireland! Galway, Ring of Kerry, (Belfast), Cork

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The irish people were very friendly and it is easy to adapt.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: A good way to socialize with local students would be trough the clubs and societies.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing in particular

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The international friendships

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Eventhough it is close to Copenhagen the university is very different
2. keep an open mind
3. Try and keep up to date with everything that is going on

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Housing can be very tricky, so if you get offered something by the campus - take it.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: It was something very special to be able to work with a real research group. Additionally, a lot of international friendships

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To live with people that maybe haven't tried to live out before (but no major challenge)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
